label: Data story

kinds.title: Opening card for the numbers.
kinds.stat: One big number that counts up, with an optional up or down change.
kinds.bars: A ranking: one bar per item, growing from zero.
kinds.line: A trend over time: a line chart that draws itself.
kinds.donut: Shares of a whole: a donut that fills part by part.
kinds.cta: Closing card: the one action viewers should take, with a button.
kinds.race: A ranking that changes over time: bars race to new places period by period (a bar chart race).
kinds.stripes: One colored stripe per value, cool below the average and warm above; can end as bars above and below the average.

fields.items: JSON list of bars, largest first: [{ "label": "Product A", "value": 31200 }]; with series, add "value2" to each. On bars an item may set "tone": "up" (green) or "down" (red) to colour its value only, e.g. the faster time.
fields.stat.text: What the number counts, e.g. "orders this week".
fields.periods: JSON list of period labels in time order, e.g. ["2005", "2010", "2015", "2020"]. 2-12 periods.
fields.series: JSON list of bars, each with one value per period: [{ "label": "Coal", "values": [2013, 1847, 1352, 774] }]. Copy every value from the source.
fields.top: How many bars show at once (3-8). The rest wait below and race in when they rank high enough.
fields.values: JSON list of numbers in time order, one stripe each (5-200), e.g. yearly temperature anomalies. Copy them from the source.
fields.stripes.labels: JSON pair: the first and the last period under the stripes, e.g. ["1880", "2025"].
fields.finish: stripes keeps the colored stripes; bars turns them into bars above and below the average at the middle of the voice line.
fields.race.vo: Give each period about a second of voice: the bars move while the line is spoken.
fields.theme: light (default), dark (the brand dark colour) or accent (the brand secondary colour). Mix them so the film is not all white.
fields.band: JSON highlight over a span of points, counted from 0: { "from": 2, "to": 2, "label": "Q3" }. Label at most 24 characters.
fields.ref: JSON dashed reference line at one value: { "value": 50, "label": "50% target" }. Label at most 24 characters. On bars (layout "columns" only) it is a dashed line across the columns, e.g. { "value": 100, "label": "Green zone" }.
fields.bars.series: Optional: two names for two bars per item, e.g. ["Commercial PEX", "Delivery PEX"]; every item then needs "value2".
fields.bars.layout: Optional: "columns" draws upright bars side by side with the value above each and the label below (good for 2-4 items with two series); default rows.
fields.bars.depth: true: the bars stand as lit 3D columns on a floor, growing one by one with the values counting above them, the camera drifting slowly round; series, tone and ref still apply, layout does not. false (default): flat bars.

description: Numbers told as a story: a title, big headline figures that count up with an up or down change, bar rankings that grow, a bar chart race over time, warming-style color stripes, a line chart that draws itself, a donut that fills in parts, then the call to action.
